diagnostic_evidence.quote: the proposed method enjoys exact entropy dissipation and unconditional stability
the inner time in the dynamic formulation is discretized using a one-step forward Euler method, making the vector field $\bu$ independent of the inner time
the JKO-based method optimizes to learn $\bu$, and the optimizer turns out to be the score
Discrete energy $\frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=1}^N |\bv_i^{n}|^2$ is conserved up to $\mathcal{O}(\tau)$.

issues.failure_explanation: After the one-step forward Euler inner discretization, the loss (djko_p2) and the update (update_v) involve only the current particles $\bv_i^n$. The learned field is the score of the current density, up to the null space, so the particle update is an explicit forward-Euler step, not an implicit one. Expanding (update_v) shows the energy increases each step by $\frac{\tau^2}{N}\sum_i|U_i|^2$. No result gives stability uniformly in $\tau$. Entropy decay (prop:added-4) holds only for the proxy $\frac1N\sum\log f^n(\bv_i^n)$, which uses a first-order Jacobian approximation, and only under exact minimization. The method instead uses SGD/Adamax on a neural network.

failure_location.quote: our method differs primarily in its design of an implicit scheme rather than an explicit one. As a result, our method is unconditionally stable and exact entropy-dissipative

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the claims to what is proved: conservation of mass and momentum, energy conservation up to $O(\tau)$, and decay of the discrete entropy proxy under exact minimization. Drop the implicit/unconditional-stability claims, or supply a stability analysis of the fully discrete scheme.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised advantages over score-based explicit methods (implicitness, unconditional stability, exact entropy decay) are unsupported for the scheme actually implemented.
issues.title: Implicitness and unconditional stability of the implemented scheme are claimed but not established
issues.why_classification: No formal result fails, but a central advertised property must be withdrawn or newly proved. That is more than a local wording fix, yet the paper's formal content survives.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Consequently, the total computational cost per epoch is significantly reduced to $\mathcal{O}(N)$.

issues.failure_explanation: Each step sums over the $B^2$ pairs in $C_q$, so it costs $O(B^2)$, not $O(BN)$. With the stated $O(BN)$ per step, the $N/B$ steps of an epoch would cost $O(N^2)$, contradicting the claimed $O(N)$ per epoch. The correct epoch cost is $O(BN)$, which is linear in $N$ only for fixed $B$.

failure_location.quote: Thus the cost of one gradient descent decreases to $\mathcal{O}(BN)$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State $O(B^2)$ per step and $O(BN)$ per epoch, which is $O(N)$ for fixed $B$.
issues.overall_effect: The complexity justification for the stochastic method is internally inconsistent.
issues.title: Inconsistent per-step and per-epoch cost of the batched SGD
issues.why_classification: A local correction preserves the advertised linear-in-$N$ cost.

issues.failure_explanation: Multiplying the coefficient $\frac{\alpha L^2B}{2N}$ by the Lemma sgd_lemma1 bound gives $\frac{\alpha^3L^2N}{2B}(\cdots)$. The proof drops the factor $B$ and writes $\frac{\alpha^3L^2N}{2B^2}(\cdots)$. Done correctly, the stepsize condition still suffices, but the variance term becomes $6\sigma^2L^2\alpha^2 N/B$, which is $B$ times larger than stated.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redo the combination step and replace $\frac{N}{B^2}$ by $\frac{N}{B}$ (and correspondingly $\frac{3\alpha^3\sigma^2L^2N}{2B}$) in the proof and statement.
issues.overall_effect: The theorem's noise floor is understated by a factor $B$.
issues.title: Factor B dropped when combining the lemmas; stated variance term too small
issues.why_classification: The fix is local, but it necessarily weakens the stated bound by a factor of the batch size, so content is lost.
